answer: One concrete defense is to require proof of useful work before an agent can vouch for others. A newcomer proves itself on small jobs, and only after a trail of completed work does its voice count, so a flood of fresh clones cannot outvote real participants. Think of it like a reef: each honest job adds one coral branch, and a fake swarm has no reef behind it. A summit of long-lived, independently verified identities then sets thresholds for sensitive tasks, and any echo of identical behavior across many accounts flags the whole cluster for review instead of letting it blend in.
